hero.title: When efficiency and leadership must work hand in hand
hero.intro:
Where transformations or M&A integrations stall, the issue is usually not the concept, but the balance between leadership and reliability. We moderate these critical transitions and make collaboration effective again in complex phases.

In this way, we create the framework for mid-sized industrial companies in which clarity emerges, responsibility is assumed, and culture and identity provide orientation in everyday operations.

services.title: Effective change
services.intro:
Our formats combine leadership, structure and operational execution. Depending on the situation, we work selectively to create clarity, in a rhythm to steer execution, or continuously to anchor change in daily operations.

Especially in critical phases such as cultural integration during M&A or succession planning, we secure the operational effectiveness of your organization through moderated transitions.

approach.title: Approach
approach.intro: Our approach is clearly structured and consistently focused on execution in day-to-day operations. We work with leadership, clarify decisions, and embed change where routines, collaboration and accountability create impact.
principles: We work within ongoing operations: Together with leadership, we design clear roles as well as decision-making and steering rhythms, enabling responsibility to be effectively assumed.
We make impact measurable: Together, we define relevant metrics, standards, and routines and embed their follow-up through leadership and decision-making routines.
We anchor change sustainably: We integrate new ways of working into routines, collaboration, as well as culture and identity.

how.title: From trigger to execution — in three steps.

about.title: About
about.heroSubtitle: Supporting leadership and organization in everyday industrial practice
intro: More than 25 years of operational industry and leadership experience are combined with technical, business, and economic-psychological expertise. Change-Werkstatt supports industrial mid-sized companies where concepts exist but fail to take effect in day-to-day operations, and where efficiency, leadership, and organizational culture need to evolve together.

The core strength lies in connecting operational reality with management perspective, enabling change to be implemented in a sustainable and effective way, especially in critical transition situations.
about.profileText:
Acceptance emerges where language, reality, and responsibility align.

In M&A, integration, and transformation situations, implementation rarely fails due to formal targets, but rather because of hidden cultural and identity-related tensions. Multilingual access to organizations and academic engagement with these dynamics make it possible to identify such tensions early, before they translate into operational or political consequences.

My work is grounded in firsthand experience across shop floor, leadership, and management roles within industrial environments. This leads to a clear guiding principle:
Change must fit operational reality, be taken up by leadership, and be embedded in everyday work.

This is how implementation emerges—without the need for explanation, because it is supported and lived.
bullets: 25+ years of operative practical experience, from industrial mechanic to cross-site head of production & logistics
Sound experience in industrial process and work organization along the value chain
Business and organizational psychology education · Focus: Leadership and Organization
Multilingualism in leadership and implementation (German · English · Turkish · Spanish · Arabic)
Ongoing Doctorate (DBA) on M&A integration, culture & identity in industrial SMEs

speaking.title: Talks & Teaching
speaking.intro: In talks and teaching formats, I address leadership, change, and operational reality. Not from a theoretical distance, but grounded in lived responsibility within organizational practice. The aim is to provide orientation, put situations into context, and create clarity for concrete decision-making.

topics.title: Efficiency and Culture in Balance
topics.subtitle: Why transformations fail — and what makes them work
topics.description: Transformation is never purely technical; it is always cultural as well. When strategies fail in everyday reality, it is often the tension between efficiency pressure and loss of identity. This talk shows how to connect both perspectives so change is not only designed, but understood and carried in daily operations.

topics.title: Shopfloor Leadership
topics.subtitle: Leading through rhythm, not firefighting
topics.description: Impact is created where value is produced. When shopfloor leadership is replaced by constant firefighting, stability is lost. I show how clear routines, meaningful metrics, and a reliable leadership cadence create orientation — and make accountability effective where problems actually arise.

topics.title: Lean Management
topics.subtitle: Daily impact instead of a toolbox obsession
topics.description: Lean is not a toolbox; it is a logic of simplification and learning. Many initiatives fail not because methods are missing, but because they do not fit daily reality. This impulse focuses on a few levers that stabilize standards, problem solving, and collaboration — without ‘method hunting’.

topics.title: M&A Integration
topics.subtitle: Culture, identity, and the operating model before and after the deal
topics.description: The economic success of mergers is decided after closing — in collaboration, leadership, and identity. Drawing on practice and DBA research, I highlight how culture and identity can be addressed early and how an operating model can be shaped to protect performance without destroying the cultural DNA that made the business successful.

topics.title: Change Governance
topics.subtitle: Decide, communicate, embed
topics.description: Change needs a clear frame; otherwise ambiguity and friction take over. Change governance is the operating system of transformation: decision paths, roles, cadence, and communication. This talk shows how to build governance pragmatically so decisions stick, communication builds trust, and new ways of working don’t fade out.

topics.title: Leadership in Transition
topics.subtitle: Role, impact, accountability
topics.description: In transformation phases, expectations on leaders shift markedly: from subject-matter expert to a builder of orientation, accountability, and collaboration. I reflect on how leadership stays effective under uncertainty, how roles are clarified, and how accountability is placed where it truly matters in daily operations.

formats: Seminar series or modular program (2–4 modules)
Teaching formats at universities and academies
speaking.ctaText: Talks provide orientation, sharpen understanding and offer a valuable starting point. Sustainable impact, however, only emerges when leadership and execution are carried forward into day-to-day operations.
